country.name: Ethiopia
country.tagline: Aksumite vines, honey wine and a French-owned estate in the Rift Valley that harvests twice a year.

stats.note: Two main wineries: Awash and Castel's Rift Valley estate.

country.overview: Ethiopia has an ancient taste for fermented drinks: tej, a honey wine flavoured with gesho leaves, is the national drink, and inscriptions and carvings from the kingdom of Aksum (third and fourth centuries AD) suggest grape wine was known there. Modern grape wine began with the Awash Winery in Addis Ababa, founded in 1956 and long the country's main producer. In the 2000s the French Castel group, invited by the government, planted vineyards in the Central Rift Valley near Ziway (Batu), about 160 km south of the capital at about 1,600 m, and launched its Rift Valley wines in 2014. Near the equator vines do not go dormant, so two harvests a year are possible; the dry season provides the better one.

history.title: Aksumite wine
history.text: Inscriptions of King Ezana and carvings on Aksum's obelisks have been read as evidence of viticulture in the Aksumite kingdom.

history.title: Awash Winery
history.text: Awash Winery was founded in Addis Ababa and became Ethiopia's main wine producer.

history.title: Castel's Rift Valley wines
history.text: Castel's estate near Ziway released its first Rift Valley wines, sold locally and exported, notably to China.

country.climate_soils: Highland tropical climate; the Rift Valley floor near Ziway has about 650 mm of rain, sandy volcanic soils and average temperatures around 25 degrees C.

sites.name: Castel Rift Valley vineyards, Ziway
sites.text: The French Castel group's estate on the floor of the Central Rift Valley near Lake Ziway and the town of Batu, planted in the 2000s on sandy volcanic soils at about 1,600 m. Its Rift Valley wines, launched in 2014, include Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot and Chardonnay; vines can be harvested twice a year.

sites.name: Awash Winery, Addis Ababa
sites.text: Founded in 1956, Awash is Ethiopia's oldest commercial winery, known for the semi-sweet red Gouder and the dry red Axumit, and for many years the country's only significant producer.
